evidence.dominant_driver: Bullock says unemployment at 4.5%-5.0% could ease inflation pressure, rising global neutral rates are lifting real yields, and she is not indicating a policy shift; the board decides policy.

market_expectations.expected_value: A September RBA hike is already priced at roughly 90-95%.
market_expectations.distribution_notes: This follow-up does not materially increase the already-high hike probability.

absorption.reason: The RBA hike theme was already heavily priced before the follow-up; AUS200/SPI entered the session slightly higher and AUD was little changed.

observations.VIX: risk-on/low-volatility carryover; no fresh exact print
observations.interpretation: Local rates remain restrictive/hawkish, but equities and AUD show no fresh risk-off confirmation and lower oil/global yields offset the rate channel.

evidence.decision_notes: Leakage-safe M2 learning: low-confidence MIXED is ACTIONABLE and strong at 15m/1h; 1h directional confidence 5-6 is ACTIONABLE REDUCE_OR_AVOID. This supports staying neutral rather than forcing a directional call.

regimes.rates: local yields elevated; US yields eased

immediate.rationale: The follow-up is nearly an hour old and explicitly denies a policy shift; the residual impulse is weak.

next_session.rationale: The new remarks soften the earlier hawkish interpretation without clearly changing the expected RBA decision.

15m.rationale: The follow-up is nearly an hour old and explicitly denies a policy shift; the residual impulse is weak.

1h.rationale: Higher neutral rates are hawkish, but higher unemployment would ease inflation and Bullock says the board decides next week.

4h.rationale: RBA hike risk is already heavily priced while lower oil/global yields support equities.

next_session.rationale: The new remarks soften the earlier hawkish interpretation without clearly changing the expected RBA decision.

predictions.mechanism: Higher neutral rates can pressure valuations, while a softer labor market could reduce inflation and future tightening needs.
predictions.invalidation: A sharp rise in Australian front-end yields with AUD strength and AUS200 breaking session support would shift the balance bearish; a clear dovish repricing would shift it bullish.
predictions.counter_case: If markets interpret the unemployment comment as a meaningful path to lower inflation, rate-hike expectations could ease and support equities.
